alternatives.root_cause: flagd's event stream to fraud-detection fails, breaking the flagged code path in fraud-detection.
alternatives.why_not: flagd's error ratio is flat and below baseline (tr_c7ffb8ffbc4d), and the only erroring fraud-detection span is a 600s event stream closing on server-side timeout (tr_0441a3299765), which is the normal lifecycle of a long-lived stream rather than a failing flag path.

alternatives.root_cause: currency became unavailable or slow, and checkout failed waiting on it.
alternatives.why_not: currency served sub-millisecond conversions throughout the observed traces (tr_06a8624b2283) with no latency growth; its absence of span-metric samples (tr_b423cd92571a) spans the baseline window too, so it is an instrumentation gap, not an outage.

alternatives.root_cause: fraud-detection's process stopped consuming while its socket stayed open.
alternatives.why_not: fraud-detection kept writing consumption lines through 06:11 (tr_a360dee3e4a7), so it was running and not silent; its gaps in traffic point upstream to missing orders.

verdict.summary: An automated environment edit set checkout's CURRENCY_ADDR to currencyservice:7001 — a wrong endpoint for the currency service — and the last application of it at 06:11 was never reverted, so checkout's currency-conversion path in the order flow broke and downstream order volume collapsed around the 06:15 onset.
verdict.reasoning: checkout's change log (tr_f3e859ef2e34) shows a repeating apply/revert cycle of a single environment value, CURRENCY_ADDR=currencyservice:7001, by platform-automation; the applications at 05:20 and 05:49 were each reverted, but the 06:11:07 application was still in place at the 06:15:16 onset. fraud-detection's error ratio (tr_4981bfabb07a) has change points at 05:53:31 and 06:15:31 — each within minutes of an applied CURRENCY_ADDR edit — and the same window contains intervals with no traffic at all, which for an order-stream consumer means checkout stopped publishing orders rather than that fraud-detection itself broke. fraud-detection's change log is empty (tr_f3892c5e1302) and its only erroring span is a long-lived flagd event stream that closes on a server-side timeout (tr_0441a3299765), while flagd's error ratio is flat and slightly below baseline (tr_c7ffb8ffbc4d), so flagd is not the mechanism. currency produced no span-metric samples in either window (tr_b423cd92571a) yet pre-06:11 traces show checkout→currency conversions completing in under a millisecond (tr_06a8624b2283), so currency was healthy and the wrongness lies in the address checkout was told to use, not in the dependency. A configuration value that names the wrong endpoint, whose wrongness is itself the failure, is bad_config rather than bad_deploy or dependency_latency.
open_questions: checkout emitted no log lines over the whole window (tr_b9efd1a93974), so there is no direct confirmation of a connection refusal or name-resolution failure against the configured address.

checkout's own error ratio stayed flat against baseline (tr_0b89452b1770), which the wrong-address story does not fully explain — the failure may surface as absent order publishes rather than errored checkout spans.
No trace sample was returned from after 06:11, so the post-change call path through checkout was not observed directly.
Why platform-automation keeps re-applying this value, and what the correct currency endpoint is, was not established.
